tierWindow.goal: Treat reflective practice as professional practice: use structured reflection to critically examine and develop your own practice, and articulate what you learn in the register a profession expects of a graduate.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Critical evaluation, synthesis and justification (appraise, critique, integrate and theorise about your own practice), not recall or guided application.
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Ill-defined, open problems drawn from your own experience; competing interpretations of an episode held together and weighed.
tierWindow.autonomy: Low scaffolding; the learner directs the reflection, sets the criteria for a good reflection, and defends their developmental conclusions.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already knows what reflection is and why it matters (the introductory tier) and can run a structured reflective cycle (the intermediate tier). They are late in their degree, likely on placement or approaching graduation, and are expected to own reflection as continuing professional development: self-directed, critical, and written for a professional reader.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, reflection as professional practice: why reflection is the engine of self-regulated professional development. Second, structured critical reflection: using Kolb's Experiential Learning Cycle to reflect critically rather than descriptively. Third, critical reflective writing: putting that reflection into writing that evaluates your practice and justifies how you will develop. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This course treats reflective practice as a professional practice. By now you know what reflection is and can run a reflective cycle; this course is about how a graduate owns and sustains reflection across a career. By the end you will be able to articulate how reflective practice drives self-regulated professional development, use a structured cycle to examine your experience critically, and produce critical reflective writing that evaluates your practice and justifies how you will develop.

These are not abstract study skills. Appraisal, supervision, revalidation and continuing professional development all rest on the same discipline, in every profession. Owning it now changes how you learn from what you do, for the rest of your career.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: articulate how reflection drives professional development, use a structured cycle to reflect critically, produce critical reflective writing.

practiceConnection.academic: Reflective practice is the habit professional life is built on. Every appraisal, every supervision conversation, every revalidation or CPD record draws on the same discipline you will build here: examining your own practice honestly, weighing it, and acting on what you find. Build it now and it carries into every placement and every year of your career.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Reflective practice is no longer something you do for a module; it is a professional discipline you can own. You can articulate why reflection drives self-regulated professional development and what sustaining it asks of you. You can take an experience and run it through Kolb's cycle to reach a reasoned plan, rather than stopping at a description. And you can put that reflection into writing that evaluates your practice and justifies how you will develop. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, reflective practice belongs to your professional life. Each placement debrief, each appraisal, each supervision conversation and CPD entry is the same discipline at work: examining your practice honestly, weighing it against the standards of your field, and acting on what you find. The graduates who keep developing are the ones who keep reflecting critically, and who can show, in writing, that they do.
